idiom_name: callback table in a struct + one fixed driver function (qsort / fopencookie shape)
implementation_notes: C has neither classes nor inheritance, so the skeleton is an ordinary function and every varying step is a function pointer stored in a struct together with the state it needs (the "cookie" that plays the role of the subclass instance). The driver calls read/transform/emit in a fixed order and a concrete processor is built by installing its own functions. libc uses the same shape wherever the algorithm is fixed and the caller supplies one step: qsort() fixes the sorting algorithm and calls your compar, and fopencookie() drives the stream protocol through the read/write/seek/close hooks in cookie_io_functions_t. The class hierarchy is therefore replaced by a pointer table plus a fixed driver - a hand-built structure that is the only realization C offers; it is still the right choice when one algorithm must serve many pluggable implementations, but it must be built and documented by hand because nothing in the language checks it.
pitfalls: An unset function pointer in the table turns the next call into a crash and the compiler cannot see it: validate the whole table at the start of the driver, or install a complete table in every constructor-like factory function.
The struct is the vtable, so adding a step changes its layout: every processor compiled against the old header must be rebuilt, and a stale object silently keeps calling the old skeleton.

State travels through the explicit void * argument or through globals; globals make the shared skeleton non-reentrant and thread-unsafe, so keep one static const table per concrete type and pass the cookie explicitly.
Nothing stops a caller from invoking a step directly and bypassing the order the driver enforces - the skeleton is only as strong as the header discipline that keeps the table private.
